Drive track inspection drawing showing the rear track and a gauge or tool at the rear; inset shows the tool shape.
Close-up drawing of the snowmobile drive track tread pattern with repeating lugs.
Track and slide runner diagram with callout 1 pointing to the runner and inset 2 showing a cross-section and wear limit measurement arrow.
Ski runner inspection diagram showing the ski underside, bolts, and two detail insets labeled A and B with callout 1 at the runner edge.
Steering system check drawing showing handlebar movement arrows, ski pivot arrows, and a vertical arrow at the steering post.
Battery level diagram with labels UPPER LEVEL and LOWER LEVEL on the side of a rectangular battery.
Close-up drawing of hands pressing a small control or latch on the end of a handlebar grip, with a downward arrow.
Handlebar control drawing with an inset showing a raised switch or button and an upward arrow, plus callout 1.
Detail A of a lever or choke control showing positions 1, 2, and 4 along a curved range of motion.
Detail B of a lever or choke control showing positions 1, 2, 3, and 4 along a curved range with dashed alternate lever positions.
Circular knob or control face diagram with a center line and two small dots below, labeled with callout 1.
Snowmobile rider silhouette with inset of a hand pulling or operating a starter/control; arrows and spark marks show activation.
Repeated snowmobile rider diagram showing a hand operating the same starter or control in the inset, with arrows and spark marks.
Line diagram of a rotary control or choke knob with callout 1 and a curved arrow indicating movement between two dot positions; the knob has a diagonal slash through it.
Panel A line diagram of a snowmobile engine compartment. Callout 1 points to a removable or open component near a small inset showing a cap or starter-rope area; illustration number 850-009.
Panel B line diagram of an engine compartment with a lifted cover or component and an inset showing a cap or rope pocket; illustration number 846-023.
Line drawing of a handlebar throttle grip or starter control with callout 1 pointing to the grip assembly and attached cable; illustration number 850-001.
Line drawing of a drive belt or clutch area with callouts 1 and 2 pointing to components near the belt guard or bracket; illustration number 850-002.
Line drawing of a drive belt area with a large component being lifted upward and a small inset showing a cable or clip; illustration number 850-003.
Two-panel close-up of a drive belt or clutch rim showing before and after positions of a cable or rope around the wheel; illustration number 850-004.
Line drawing showing a hand pulling an emergency starter rope upward beside a belt or pulley assembly, with arrows and a star symbol indicating the pull action; illustration number 850-005.
Line diagram of a rotary control knob with callout 1 and a curved arrow between two dot positions; the knob is shown with a vertical bar through its center.
Rider on a snowmobile with an inset pointing to a control switch near the handlebar. A bold arrow indicates pressing or moving the switch; illustration number 815-006.
Line drawing of a rider seated forward on a snowmobile climbing uphill; the snowmobile is angled upward on a slope; illustration number 852-002.
Line drawing of a rider standing or leaning back on a snowmobile descending a slope, with snow spray behind; illustration number 852-003.
Rear view of a rider on a snowmobile traversing a side slope near trees, with a downward arrow indicating body position or direction; illustration number 852-004.
Black warning label with a triangular exclamation icon and the word WARNING in white uppercase letters.
Panel A line drawing of a control lever near the dashboard, with callout 1 and a bold arrow showing the lever being moved to the right; illustration number 817-012.
Panel A line drawing of the same control lever area, with callout 2 and a bold arrow showing the lever being moved left or downward; illustration number 817-013.
Panel B drawing showing a handlebar-mounted switch or lever being lifted upward. A side inset lists positions 1, 2, and 3 beside a control panel; illustration number 817-004.

Multi-part diagram. Top panels A and B show two rotary knob positions with callout 1 and curved arrows; bottom panel shows a small rectangular part being pressed down into a handlebar control; illustration number 831-046 and 831-021.
Panel A engine-compartment line drawing with callout 1 pointing to a component or connector near the starter or intake area; illustration number 846-015.
Panel B engine-compartment line drawing with callout 1 pointing to a rectangular electrical or mechanical unit mounted near the chassis; illustration number 846-021.
Panel C engine-compartment line drawing with callout 1 pointing to a mesh-covered or finned component near cables and hoses; illustration number 846-020.
Panel D line drawing of a compartment edge with callout 1 pointing to a small rectangular connector or cable fitting; illustration number 846-006.
Text specification box reading Spark plug reach 1: BR250T 12.7 mm (0.50 in); CS340E/ET410TR/VK540E 19.0 mm (0.75 in).
Technical line drawing of a spark plug tip with measurement arrows. Callout 1 marks plug reach or thread length and callout 2 marks the electrode gap; illustration number 834-001.
Panel A carburetor or engine detail drawing with callout 1 pointing to a top screw, cable, or adjuster near the intake; illustration number 804-014.
Panel B engine detail drawing with callout 1 pointing to an adjuster or fitting among several cables and hoses; illustration number 816-031.
Panel C engine detail drawing with callout 1 pointing to a spring-loaded adjuster or cable fitting near hoses; illustration number 816-029.
Panel D carburetor detail drawing with callout 1 pointing to a knob or screw on the carburetor body; illustration number 804-018.
Panel A split drawing showing throttle lever free play at the handlebar with callout 1, and an engine-side adjuster with callouts 2 and 3; illustration number 816-028.
Panel B split drawing showing throttle lever free play at callout 1 and an engine-side cable adjuster with callouts 2 and 3; illustration number 816-032.
Panel C split drawing showing throttle lever free play at callout 1 and a spring/cable adjuster area with callouts 2 and 3; illustration number 816-034.
Panel D split drawing showing throttle lever free play at callout 1 and an engine-side linkage or cable adjuster with callouts 2 and 3; illustration number 816-017.
Text specification box for throttle lever free play. It lists BR250T/ET410TR/VK540E: 1.0 - 2.0 mm (0.04 - 0.08 in) and CS340E: 0.5 - 1.0 mm (0.02 - 0.04 in).
Panel A line drawing of a hand adjusting a carburetor linkage or cable. Callouts 1, 2, and 3 point to the adjuster, locknut, and related part; illustration number 800-011.
Panel B line drawing of a hand adjusting a cable or screw near hoses and a spring-loaded component. Callouts 1, 2, and 3 identify the parts; illustration number 800-018.
Panel C line drawing of a cable adjuster area with callouts 1, 2, and 3 pointing to fittings and a spring or plunger; illustration number 816-041.
Panel D line drawing of a cable adjuster beside an engine component, with callouts 1, 2, and 3 marking the adjuster, locknut, and related fitting; illustration number 800-008.
Panel A carburetor line drawing with callout 3 pointing to a top screw or adjustment point near the intake and linkages; illustration number 804-036.
Panel B engine top view showing spark plug or cable openings and surrounding bolts, with a hand or tool at the lower edge; illustration number 804-032.
Panel C close-up line drawing of a small adjustment screw or hook-shaped tool near cables, with illustration number 804-017.
Text box giving standard pilot screw positions: BR250T/VK540E 1 1/4, CS340E 1 1/2, ET410TR 1 3/8 turns out from the seated position.
Pilot screw adjustment table. Turning in makes the mixture leaner for warmer weather or higher altitude; turning out makes it richer for colder weather or lower altitude.
Snowmobile carburetor service drawing labeled with a panel letter, showing a close-up adjustment point or screw circled on the carburetor area with reference number.
Snowmobile carburetor service drawing labeled with a panel letter, showing a close-up adjustment point or screw circled on the carburetor area with reference number.
Snowmobile carburetor service drawing labeled with a panel letter, showing a close-up adjustment point or screw circled on the carburetor area with reference number.
Text box listing standard main jet numbers: BR250T #105, CS340E #174, ET410TR #166, and VK540E #141.3.
Main jet adjustment table. Smaller number gives leaner mixture for warmer weather or higher altitude; larger number gives richer mixture for colder weather or lower altitude.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Cross-section drawing of a drive pulley or sheave, with a callout pointing to the belt position or spacer area.
Belt width and spacer position table comparing ET410TR and VK540E belt widths with spacer positions of 2 spacers, 1 spacer, or no spacer between sheaves.
Belt width limits table. New belt width is ET410TR 31.6 mm (1.24 in) and VK540E 35 mm (1.38 in). Belt wear limit width is ET410TR 28 mm (1.10 in) and VK540E 32 mm (1.26 in).
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Drive belt and clutch service drawing showing a belt around a sheave or pulley, hands moving the belt, and numbered arrows for removal or installation steps.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Oil level table. It says slight flow from the level bolt hole means oil level CORRECT; no flow means insufficient.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Text box specifying drive chain oil: API GL-3, SAE 75 or 80.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Gearcase or chaincase service illustration with a labeled panel, numbered callouts, and bolts, covers, plugs, or adjustment parts indicated.
Brake lever or bracket side-view drawing with a small dimension marked 1 near the tip or contact surface.
Brake adjustment diagram showing a brake lever, pad or cable section, spring, and adjuster bolt with multiple numbered callouts.
Brake adjustment diagram showing a brake lever, pad or cable section, spring, and adjuster bolt with multiple numbered callouts.
Handlebar brake lever free play diagram with a downward arrow on the lever and a gap marked 9 at the lever pivot.
Vertical cross-section or gauge drawing with dimension callout 1 between two parallel surfaces.
Brake cable or handlebar lever adjustment drawing with callouts 1 and 2 on a cable adjuster near a brake lever.
Brake adjustment diagram showing a brake lever, pad or cable section, spring, and adjuster bolt with multiple numbered callouts.
Handlebar brake lever free play diagram with a downward arrow and a gap marked 7 at the lever pivot.
Repeat vertical gauge or cross-section drawing with dimension callout 1.
Suspension or engine mount adjustment illustration with a bolt callout and a small inset showing numbered adjustment directions.
Suspension or engine mount adjustment illustration with a bolt callout and a small inset showing numbered adjustment directions.
Table for rear suspension spring seat position. Columns show positions 1, 2, and 3; preload changes from Harder to Softer, and the standard position is 2.
Diagram A of a snowmobile suspension spring adjuster. It shows a tool at callout 1 and an inset scale with notches numbered 1 through 5.
Diagram B of a rear suspension spring adjuster. It shows callout 1 on the adjuster and an inset scale with notches numbered 2 through 7.
Snowmobile suspension diagram showing a spring and wheel assembly. Callouts 1 and 2 point to an adjuster area and a measured gap or length near the spring.
Table for spring adjuster position A, standard front. Positions 1 through 5 are shown; preload changes from Softer to Harder, and standard front position is 3.
Table for spring adjuster position B, standard rear. Positions 1 through 7 are shown; preload changes from Softer to Harder, and standard rear position is 4.
Adjuster table. Turning the adjuster in makes preload harder and suits icy snow condition; turning out makes preload softer and suits soft snow condition. Standard length 2 is 16 mm (0.63 in).
Installation position table for suspension settings. Positions C, B, and A correspond to hard, medium, and soft spring rate and damping; standard is A.
Suspension installation diagram showing the rear arm or link with an inset labeled A, B, and C. Callout 1 points to the selected mounting hole.
Adjustment diagram showing a toothed adjuster wheel rotated upward by arrow 1 and a bolt or adjuster component labeled 2.
Suspension rod adjustment diagram with callouts 1 and 2 at the rod ends, arrows through the links, and small B labels near each adjuster.
Track deflection measurement diagram. It shows the lower track run with callout 1 indicating the measured clearance and callout 2 showing a hanging spring scale or weight pulling downward.
Rear wheel or idler wheel diagram with callout 1 pointing to the center axle or fastener.
Track inspection diagram showing a snowmobile lifted from below and a track section with several contact points labeled 3.
Rear track adjustment diagram showing the idler wheel area with callouts 4 and 5 on left and right adjusters.
Track alignment diagrams labeled 6 and 7. They show a track shifted to one side relative to guide lugs, with callouts 8 through 12 marking clearances and track parts.

Track alignment correction table. If track alignment 6 is shifted to right, left adjuster 4 turns out and right adjuster 5 turns in. If 7 is shifted to left, left adjuster turns in and right adjuster turns out.
Rear axle assembly diagram showing bolts, washers, spacers, and end pieces with callouts 13, 14, 15, and 16. Insets show hook-shaped clips or retainers.
Rear track adjustment diagram showing the idler wheel area with left and right adjusters labeled 4 and 5.
Track deflection correction table. For more than specified deflection, left adjuster 4 and right adjuster 5 turn in. For less than specified, both adjusters turn out.
Rear wheel or idler wheel diagram with callouts 1 and 2 pointing to the axle nut and central fastener or washer.
Track inspection diagram showing a snowmobile lifted from below and a track section with several contact points labeled 3.
Rear track diagram viewed from behind, with callouts 4 and 5 pointing to the left and right adjuster bolts.
Track alignment diagrams labeled 6 and 7, showing track shift direction and clearances with numbered callouts 8 through 12.
Rear track diagram viewed from behind, with callouts 4 and 5 pointing to left and right adjuster locations.
Track alignment table. Shifted to right: left adjuster turns out and right adjuster turns in. Shifted to left: left adjuster turns in and right adjuster turns out.
Track deflection table. More than specified: left and right adjusters turn in. Less than specified: left and right adjusters turn out.
Rear axle tightening torque table. CS340E/ET410TR: 75 Nm (7.5 m-kg, 55 ft-lb). VK540E: 80 Nm (8.0 m-kg, 58 ft-lb).
Top-view ski alignment diagram showing two skis with dimension arrows labeled 1 at the front and 2 at the rear.
Measurement text for ski toe-out: Ski toe-out (1 - 2): 0 to 15 mm (0.0 to 0.6 in).
Steering adjustment diagrams. The upper view shows the handlebar area; the lower view shows a linkage or block with dimension a and a prime mark, plus callout 1 and arrow 2.
Handlebar cover or cowling diagram with callout 1 pointing to two screws or fasteners near the handlebar base.
Close-up diagram of the steering column or handlebar base with hoses and fasteners around an opening.
Linkage alignment diagram showing two blocks and a central round opening. It labels dimension a on the left and a prime on the right, with arrow 2 indicating direction.
Diagram A showing a hand working near a cable, hose, or connector behind a vertical frame member; a long arrow indicates pulling or routing direction.
Diagram B showing a cable or hose connector near a vertical frame member, with an arrow pointing to the connector area.
Diagram C showing the handlebar and steering post area, with a hand pulling or adjusting a cable at the center.
Close-up of a handlebar or brake/throttle cable assembly. Callout 1 points to an adjuster or fastener near a cable end.
Diagram A showing a suspension or steering bracket from above, with callout 2 and an upward arrow indicating the part position.
Diagram B showing a suspension link or bracket with callout 3 pointing to a spring or fastener at the joint.
Diagram B showing the full snowmobile track and rear suspension assembly from the side. Callout 4 points near the rear suspension area and the track path is drawn through multiple wheels.
Headlight bulb or lamp socket diagram. Callout 1 points to the bulb base or connector on the rear of the lamp housing.
Lamp socket removal diagram showing an arrow pointing left from the rear of a bulb socket on a housing.
Diagram A showing a small headlight bulb with its mounting flange and electrical prongs.
Diagram B showing a round bulb with a flange and electrical prongs, drawn separately from the vehicle.
Lamp housing diagram with four fasteners around a rectangular light lens. Callout 1 points to the screws or mounting points.
Two-part bulb replacement diagram. The upper panel shows a lamp connector or socket with callout 1; the lower panel shows a replacement bulb like the one in diagram A.
Side panel or cover diagram showing a round knob or cap on the snowmobile body. Callout 1 points to the knob.
Battery electrolyte level diagram. The battery case is labeled UPPER LEVEL and LOWER LEVEL, with callouts 1 and 2 and an arrow showing the correct level range.
Electrical component diagram showing a hand removing or installing a small relay or fuse-like part from a connector block.
Diagram A showing a hand holding a small component near the engine or carburetor area, likely a drain or inspection part.
Diagram B showing a hand tool or cable near a vertical engine area, with the component being adjusted or routed.
Diagram C showing a hand working among hoses and wiring near the engine compartment, with a circled detail area.

Snowmobile electrical wiring schematic with numbered components 1 through 23, switches, connector blocks, lamps, ignition or charging components, ground symbols, and wire paths labeled with color abbreviations such as B, L, R, W, Y/R, B/W, G/Y, and B/Y. The diagram shows the harness routing between handlebar controls, switch blocks, battery or electrical modules, lamps, and ground connections.

Snowmobile electrical wiring schematic with numbered components 1 through 25. It shows switch blocks with OFF, ON/LIGHT, START, RUN, HI, LO, and OFF/ON positions, connector groups, lamps or loads, ground points, coil or regulator symbols, and wire paths labeled with color abbreviations including B, L, R, W, Y/R, B/W, B/Y, G/Y, and O.

Snowmobile electrical wiring schematic with numbered components 1 through 28. It includes handlebar or instrument components, switch tables for OFF, ON/LIGHT, START, RUN, HI, and LO positions, connector blocks, wire harness paths, ground symbols, a coil or transformer symbol, and multiple color-coded wires labeled with abbreviations such as B, L, P, G, Y, R, W, B/W, G/Y, B/Y, and Y/R.
